items.title: Declarations of Pecuniary Interest under the “Municipal Conflict of Interest Act”
Rick Chambers and Marcia Smellie, Waterloo Region Age Friendly Network
notes:
Rick Chambers and Marcia Smellie appeared on behalf of the Waterloo Region Age Friendly Network to request free ridership on GRT for children under 12 and adults over 65 on Wednesdays and Sundays. R. Chambers stated that Wednesdays and Sundays were chosen as a result of a survey and provided comparisons to other transit services, such as British Columbia and Ottawa. He noted the social and environmental reasons for this request, such as reducing congestion on roads, building the ridership of the future, and reducing isolation. R. Chambers concluded by asking that staff be directed to look at the cost of a project pilot for free ridership for children under 12 and adults over 65 on Wednesdays and Sundays. 

A copy of their presentation is attached to the minutes. 

The Committee discussed the request and presentation, including the benefits and disadvantages of reduced fares being household income based, exploring innovative opportunities in the Townships, service levels, and impact on ridership. 

Bruce Lauckner, Chief Administrative Officer, confirmed that staff have taken direction and that this request will be reviewed during the 2023 budget process.

items.title: TSD-TRS-23-001, Laurier U-Pass Program Update
notes:
Mathieu Goetzke, Commissioner Transportation Services, introduced the report, noting that there is an upcoming referendum at Wilfrid Laurier University on January 24 and January 26th, where students will vote to continue the U-Pass program. This program enables students to have unlimited trips for a fee paid per term, as part of their tuition. He noted that staff will be supporting students on the referendum and that this will allow students to opt in or out until August 2025, in order to allow staff to complete a full review of the U-Pass program. M. Goetzke shared that the benefits of the program include unlimited trips for the students and a source of stable revenue and ridership for the Region. 

In response to the Committee, M. Goetzke confirmed that Conestoga College has expressed interest in the U-Pass program and that staff have been working with the college. 

The report was received for information.

items.title: Strategic Focus - Environmental and Climate Action
EES-WMS-23-001, Blue Box Transition Update (Staff Presentation)
notes:
Jennifer Rose, Commissioner, Engineering and Environmental Services introduced the report and presentation, noting that this is the first in a series of reports regarding how the Waste-Free Ontario Act will impact recycling services within the Region of Waterloo.

Jon Arsenault, Director, Waste Management provided a presentation, which included an outline of the changes to the existing program, producer responsibility, an overview of the common collection system model, and next steps. 

M. Harris joined the meeting at 10:49 a.m.

A copy of the presentation is attached to the minutes. The report was received for information. 

The Committee discussed the report and presentation, noting the importance of a holistic communication plan, potential opportunities, concerns regarding service levels, and life of the Region's landfill. 

In response to the Committee, J. Rose stated that the cost of waste pick up in the downtown areas is currently borne through the tax levy, and that continuing this service after the transition period will be an item for Council to consider at a later point, including any financial implications. J. Rose noted the complexity of this transition, and that staff are continuing to gather information.
